mcq.question: Why does the SMTP client send `..hidden line` when the message contains a line `.hidden line`?

options.A: A line with a single dot ends the DATA section, so leading dots are doubled (dot-stuffing) and the server removes one
options.B: To mark the line as a comment
options.C: Because SMTP forbids lines starting with a letter

mcq.explanation: The end of the message body is signalled by a line containing only '.'. Doubling a leading dot keeps body lines from being mistaken for that terminator.

mcq.question: What does the `Transport` interface make possible?

options.A: Sending email without any SMTP server
options.B: Running the same SMTP logic against a real socket, a scripted fake server in tests, or a dry run

mcq.explanation: The client only calls `send_line` and `read_reply`. Swapping the implementation behind that small interface changes where the bytes go without touching the protocol code.
